subject: Error/Warning regarding Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) and rejection of Metropolis

messages.author: c2585c52e059b919
messages.subject: Error/Warning regarding Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) and rejection of Metropolis
parts:
Hi, all,

I'm trying to estimate an ideal model that models guessing behavior based on the latent ability. It's an Random Effect IRT model. The Stan code is as below:

Bayesian_3PLAG_Model<-'data {
int<lower=0> n_student; // n_student: the number of students
int<lower=0> n_item; // n_item: the number of items
int<lower=0,upper=1> y[n_student, n_item]; // the matrix of responses patterm
}

parameters {
real mean_theta; // the mean of latent ability
real sigma_theta; // the standard deviation of latent ability
real item_diff[n_item]; // item difficulty for items
real item_disc[n_item]; // item discrimination for items
real item_omega[n_item]; // weight for how latent ability affect guessing
}

model {
// assigning prior distribution for paramaters;

  matrix[n_student, n_item] p;
  matrix[n_student, n_item] p_process;
  matrix[n_student, n_item] g_process;
  real theta[n_student];
  mean_theta ~ normal(0, 0.5);
  sigma_theta ~ normal(0, 0.5);
  theta ~ normal(mean_theta, sigma_theta);

// Likelihood:
  
  for(i in 1:n_student)
    {
      for (j in 1:n_item)
        {
          p_process[i, j] <- inv_logit(item_disc[j]*(theta[i] - item_diff[j]))
          g_process[i, j] <- (1-p_process[i, j])*inv_logit(item_omega[j]*(theta[i]));
          p[i, j] <- p_process[i, j] + g_process[i, j]
          y[i, j] ~ bernoulli(p[i, j]);
        }
    }
}
'

I got a parser warning while compiling:

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal):
Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If it does, you need to include a target += statement with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    theta ~ normal(...)

Then I got an error message shown:

[595] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                        
[596] "Exception thrown at line 26: normal_log: Random variable[1] is nan, but must not be nan!"                                              
[597] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[598] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                              
[599] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                              
[600] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                          
[601] "Initialization between (-2, 2) failed after 100 attempts. "                                                                            
[602] " Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model."                                 
[603] "Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : "                                                                                      
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

I did some search before I'm asking the question. It looks like I define the theta (the blue line) in the model block, which is a local parameter, and initialized as NA. If I move the blue line to the parameter block, then there is no problem. However, I do want the theta as a local parameter, and theta ~ N(mean_theta, sigma_theta) with hyper-parameter mean_theta, sigma_theta. so that the result can be a list as follows:

mean_theta ...
sigma_theta ...
item_diff 1 to n.items ...
item_disc 1 to n.items ...
item_omega 1 to n_items ...

But if I move the definition to the parameter block, the result gets tones of thetas like:

theta 1 to n_students ...
mean_theta ...
sigma_theta ...
item_diff 1 to n.items ...
item_disc 1 to n.items ...
item_omega 1 to n_items ...

I'm wondering how can I define the theta as a local parameter, which is a random effect with the distribution N(mean_theta, sigma_theta), without freely estimating thetas as a parameter?

I'll appreciate any help, thanks and Happy Holidays!

Sincerely,
Jiaqi

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Error/Warning regarding Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) and rejection of Metropolis
parts:
You need to declare sigma as

real<lower = 0> sigma;

All parameter values that satisfy declared constraints must
have support (finite log density [equivalently positive density])
in the model block.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Error/Warning regarding Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) and rejection of Metropolis
parts:
No. The sampling statements only increment the log
density, so all the terms used in them must be defined
before they are used.

You can use RNGs in the generated quantities block if
that's what you're trying to accomplish. Otherwise, you
just need to declare the unknowns as parameters. You can
just forget about them during inference and focus on
the marginal of the other paramters.

- Bob
